reference_action: OP switched from fast-drying terracotta to plastic and added a small mound of soil; plant perked up. Confirmed container/soil change improves moisture retention. More water was suggested but not explicitly reported as the adopted change.

sources.reason: Generic large gritty pots and future up-potting do not specify plastic/retention change; emphasizes drying and neglect.
Dry/neglect/in-ground advice omits plastic container or added moisture-retaining soil.
Explicit terracotta and coarse fast-draining mix oppose container change. Mounded gritty soil is for draining heavy ground, not retaining moisture around this potted root ball.
Fast drainage, dry upper soil and other care omit plastic or retaining more root-zone moisture.
Explicitly says unglazed terracotta, not plastic; contrary to confirmed pot change.

actions.action: Repot into large draining pot with gritty soil
Check soil 2 inches down and soak when dry
Move to full sun with temporary shade on extreme hot days
Pot on as root ball grows

resolved.reason: Accepts overwatering/neglect framing and omits the successful moisture-retaining plastic change. Grittier soil plus neglect can worsen drying in this hot terracotta setup; measured watering is a mitigating component.

harmfulness.reason: “Neglect is the best thing” and blanket tolerance of extreme cold/heat are risky for a small potted rosemary already drying in heat. Grittier soil without recognizing rapid terracotta drying can worsen the actual problem, despite the separate two-inch watering check.

specificity_accuracy.reason: “Use large well draining pots” is generic rosemary advice. It misses the documented drying extremes and successful switch to plastic, reinforcing the user’s incorrect overwatering assumption.

feasibility.reason: A two-inch soil check and soaking are concrete. “Large” and “gritty” leave pot dimensions and substrate proportions unspecified, and repeated repotting adds work without a case-specific trigger.

- generic: Use large well draining pots with gritty soil. Allow the soil to dry out down to 2 inches before watering then give it a soak. The plant will do best in full sun however on extreme hot days move it into a shade area so it will not burn. As your plant grows pot it on to allow room for the root ball.
